full_text_zh:
[P1] 手机淘宝扫一扫

那双鞋子

Maribeth Boelts
illustrated by Noah Z. Jones

CANDLEWICK PRESS

[P2] 我梦想着那双鞋子。黑色高帮。
上面两条白色斜条纹。

[P3] “奶奶，我想要那双鞋子。”
“我们不能买‘想要’的东西，只能买‘需要’的东西。”
奶奶说。“现在你需要的是一双冬天穿的新靴子。”

[P4] 布兰登·T穿着那双鞋子来到学校。他说现在我已经不是班里跑得最快的人了，他才是。在那双鞋子出现之前，我一直都是所有同学中跑得最快的。
奈特也穿着那双鞋子来到学校。安东尼奥和我一起数了数奈特上厕所的次数——一天上了七次，就为了穿着那双鞋子在学校大厅里慢悠悠地走来走去。
接着，艾伦·雅各比和特伦斯每人也有一双那样的鞋子。

[P5] 然后，有一天，我的鞋底在踢球的时候掉了。
“看来你需要一双新鞋子了，杰瑞米，”阿尔弗里老师说。
他拿出爱心箱，里边有鞋子和其他一些孩子们可能会需要的东西。他从箱子里面翻出一双我能穿的鞋子，一双维可牢搭扣鞋，跟我小表妹马歇尔穿的鞋子一样。鞋上有一个卡通人物，我估计没人看过那个动画片。

[P6] 我穿着老师给我的鞋子回到教室，艾伦·雅各比看了一眼阿尔弗里老师给我的鞋子，哈哈大笑。特伦斯、布兰登·T和其他人也笑起来。唯一一个没嘲笑我的同学是安东尼奥·帕克。

回到家，奶奶说：“阿尔弗里先生真是太好了。”我点点头，就转过身去。我才不会为一双蠢鞋子掉眼泪呢。

但当我拼写单词的时候，每个单词看起来都像“鞋子”这个词。我紧紧握住铅笔，感觉铅笔都快断了。

[P7] 星期六，奶奶说：“我们去看看你特别想要的那双鞋子吧。我存了点钱。说不定，也许够了呢。”

到了鞋店，奶奶把鞋底翻过来，看看卖多少钱。当她看到价钱的时候，沉重地坐了下来。

“也许他们写错了，”我说。奶奶摇摇头。

[P8] 然后我想起了二手商店。
“如果一个富家孩子他的鞋子穿小了，或者圣诞节收到两双
鞋子的话，他会不会送人一双呢？”
我们乘公共汽车去第一家二手商店。那里有黑色牛仔靴、粉色拖鞋、凉鞋、高跟鞋——除了我想要的那双以外什么五花
八门的鞋子都有。
我们又乘公共汽车去第二家二手商店。还是没有找到我想要
的那双鞋子。
拐角处是第三家二手商店……我看到橱窗里有个什么东西。

[P9] 黑色鞋子，上面有两条白色的斜纹。高帮。
完美。
2.50美金。
那双鞋子。
我脱下自己的旧鞋子，拽一拽宽松的袜子，心里怦怦直跳。
“太棒了！”奶奶说。“这双是多大号码的？”
我把脚伸进第一只鞋里，努力曲起脚趾，把脚后跟塞进去。
“我也不知道，但我觉得挺合适的。”

[P10] 奶奶跪在地板上，用手捏捏我的脚趾。
“哦，杰瑞米。”她说。“我可不能花那么多钱买
一双不合脚的鞋子。”

我穿上另一只鞋，站起身来走一走试试。
“挺合适的，”我屏住呼吸，祈祷我的脚趾可以掉下来。
但我的脚趾没有掉下来。
不管咋样，我还是用自己的钱买了它。我把脚挤进鞋里，
一瘸一拐地向公共汽车站走去。

[P11] 过了几天，奶奶在我的衣橱里放了一双新靴子。对于那双挤得我的脚生疼的鞋子，她什么也没说。
“有时候鞋子会越撑越大，”我对奶奶说。奶奶拥抱了我。

[P12] 我每天都注意观察，但那双鞋子一点儿也没有被撑大。
没办法，我只好又换回阿尔弗里先生给我的鞋去上学了。
一天正在上数学课，我瞥了一眼安东尼奥的鞋子。
只见他的一只鞋上裹着胶带，他的脚看起来比我小。
放学以后，我来到公园，一个人思考。
安东尼奥也在公园——他是班里唯一一个没有因为我穿着
阿尔弗里先生给的鞋而嘲笑我的同学。

[P13] 我们一起玩儿投篮——他的鞋子上有一块胶带松了，所以每次他跳起来的时候，这块胶带都会拍打一下地面。
我想，我不想这样。
我们从秋千上跳下来。
我不想这样。
我们从操场的一头跑到另外一头——
“我不想这样！”我说。
“你不想什么？”安东尼奥气喘吁吁地问我。

[P14] 奶奶叫我吃晚饭，请安东尼奥也一起来。
吃完晚饭，他突然发现了我的那双鞋子。
“你怎么不穿呢？”安东尼奥问道。
我耸耸肩。我的手心直冒汗——我能感觉到他希望
那双鞋子要是他的该有多好。
那天晚上，我想着安东尼奥说的话，久久无法入睡。
天亮了，我最后一次穿了一下那双鞋子。

[P15] 在改变主意之前，我已经把那双鞋子藏到外衣里了。
我穿过街道，一溜烟跑到安东尼奥家的公寓，这时下起雪来了。
我把鞋子放在他家门口，按响了门铃——然后扭头就跑。

[P16] 在学校，安东尼奥穿着那双崭新的鞋子，笑容满面。
看着他的笑脸，我感到好开心呀。可是看着阿尔弗里
先生给我的鞋子，我简直要抓狂。

但到下课时，发生了一件事。
到处都是厚厚的积雪。
“把你们的鞋子放在大厅里，换上靴子，”老师说道。
把你们的鞋子放在大厅里。这时，我才想起来我的书包里还有一双新靴子呢。从来没有哪个同学穿过一双一样的新靴子。
大家站成一排准备休息，这时安东尼奥凑过来对我说：“谢谢你。”

我笑了笑，轻轻推了他一下。

[P17] “我们看看谁跑得快吧！”,
full_text_en:
[P1] Scan with Taobao app

Those Shoes

Maribeth Boelts
illustrated by Noah Z. Jones

CANDLEWICK PRESS

[P2] I dream of those shoes. Black high-tops.
With two white diagonal stripes.

[P3] "Grandma, I want those shoes."
"We can't buy things we 'want,' only things we 'need,'" Grandma said. "What you need now is a new pair of winter boots."

[P4] Brandon T came to school wearing those shoes. He said I'm no longer the fastest runner in class — he is. Before those shoes appeared, I was always the fastest among all my classmates.
Nate also came to school wearing those shoes. Antonio and I counted how many times Nate went to the bathroom — seven times a day, just to walk slowly around the school cafeteria wearing those shoes.
Then, Allen Jacoby and Terence each got a pair of those shoes too.

[P5] Then, one day, the sole of my shoe fell off while I was playing soccer.
"It looks like you need a new pair of shoes, Jeremy," Mr. Alferi said.
He pulled out the kindness box, which contained shoes and other things that children might need. He rummaged through the box and found a pair I could wear—a pair of Velcro sneakers, just like the ones my little cousin Marshall wore. There was a cartoon character on them; I bet no one had seen that cartoon.

[P6] I returned to the classroom wearing the shoes the teacher gave me. Allen Jacob looked at the shoes Mr. Alfrid gave me and burst out laughing. Terence, Brandon T, and others started laughing too. The only classmate who didn't laugh at me was Antonio Park.

When I got home, Grandma said, "Mr. Alfrid is so kind." I nodded and turned away. I wouldn't cry over a pair of silly shoes.

But when I was spelling words, every word looked like the word "shoes." I gripped my pencil tightly, feeling like it might break.

[P7] On Saturday, Grandma said, “Let’s go look at the shoes you really want. I’ve saved some money. Maybe it’s enough.”

At the shoe store, Grandma turned the shoe over to see how much it cost. When she saw the price, she sat down heavily.

“Maybe they wrote it wrong,” I said. Grandma shook her head.

[P8] Then I thought of secondhand stores.
"If a rich kid's shoes get too small, or if they get two pairs for Christmas, would they give one away?"
We took the bus to the first secondhand store. There were black cowboy boots, pink slippers, sandals, high heels—everything except the pair I wanted.
We took the bus to the second secondhand store. Still no luck finding the shoes I wanted.
Around the corner was the third secondhand store... I saw something in the window.

[P9] Black shoes, with two white diagonal stripes. High-top.
Perfect.
2.50 dollars.
Those shoes.
I took off my old shoes, pulled at my loose socks, and my heart was pounding.
"Great!" Grandma said. "What size are these?"
I stuck my foot into the first shoe, strained to curl my toes, and pushed my heel in.
"I don't know, but I think they fit pretty well."

[P10] Grandma knelt on the floor, gently pinching my toes.
“Oh, Jeremy,” she said. “I can’t spend that much money on a pair of shoes that don’t fit.”

I put on the other shoe and stood up to walk around and try them on.
“Pretty comfortable,” I held my breath, praying my toes would fall off.
But my toes didn’t fall off.
Anyway, I still bought them with my own money. I squeezed my feet into the shoes and limped toward the bus stop.

[P11] A few days later, Grandma put a new pair of boots in my closet. She said nothing about the shoes that were squeezing my feet painfully.
"Sometimes shoes get bigger with wear," I told Grandma. Grandma hugged me.

[P12] I paid attention every day, but those shoes didn't get stretched at all.
There was nothing I could do, so I had to switch back to the shoes Mr. Alferi gave me to go to school.
One day during math class, I glanced at Antonio's shoes.
I saw that one of his shoes was wrapped in tape, and his feet looked smaller than mine.
After school, I came to the park to think by myself.
Antonio was also in the park—he was the only classmate who hadn't laughed at me for wearing
the shoes Mr. Alferi gave me.

[P13] We played basketball together—his shoe had a loose piece of tape, so every time he jumped, the tape would slap the ground.
I thought, I don’t want this.
We jumped off the swings.
I don’t want this.
We ran from one end of the playground to the other—
“I don’t want this!” I said.
“What don’t you want?” Antonio panted, asking me.

[P14] Grandma called me for dinner and invited Antonio to come too.
After dinner, he suddenly noticed my shoes.
"Why aren't you wearing them?" Antonio asked.
I shrugged. My palms were sweating—I could feel how much he wished
those shoes were his.
That night, I thought about what Antonio said and couldn't fall asleep for a long time.
When morning came, I put on those shoes for the last time.

[P15] Before I changed my mind, I had already hidden the shoes inside my coat.
I ran across the street, quickly reaching Antonio's apartment, just as it started to snow.
I placed the shoes at his front door, rang the doorbell—and then turned and ran away.

[P16] At school, Antonio was wearing his brand-new shoes, beaming with joy.
Seeing his smile made me so happy. But looking at the shoes Mr. Alfridi gave me, I was about to go crazy.

But then, during recess, something happened.
Everywhere was covered in thick snow.
"Put your shoes in the hall and put on your boots," the teacher said.
Put your shoes in the hall. At that moment, I remembered I had a pair of new boots in my backpack. No other classmate had ever worn a pair of identical new boots.
Everyone lined up to rest, and then Antonio came over to me and said, "Thank you."

I smiled and gently pushed him.

[P17] "Let's see who can run faster!"
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页是绘本《那双鞋子》的封面，展示了书名、作者和插画师信息，画面中两个孩子在城市街道上行走，背景是城市建筑和一棵光秃的树。
[P2] 一个背着书包的孩子站在街边，仰望着墙上一幅巨大的运动鞋广告，内心渴望着那双黑色高帮、带有两条白色斜条纹的鞋子。
[P3] 孩子向奶奶表达了对一双鞋子的渴望，奶奶则解释说他们只能买‘需要’的东西，并指出孩子真正需要的是冬天穿的新靴子。
[P4] 本页描述了班上越来越多的同学拥有了主角渴望的那双鞋子，布兰登·T、奈特、艾伦·雅各比和特伦斯都穿上了同样的鞋子，主角感到自己的独特性正在消失。
[P5] 主角的鞋底在踢球时掉了，老师阿尔弗里从爱心箱里拿出一双维可牢搭扣鞋给他，这双鞋和他小表妹穿的一样，上面有卡通人物。
[P6] 主角穿着老师给的维可牢搭扣鞋回到教室，遭到同学嘲笑，只有安东尼奥·帕克没有笑。回到家后，奶奶称赞老师，主角强忍情绪，但在写作业时因心事重重而感到痛苦。
[P7] 奶奶答应带孩子去鞋店看那双他特别想要的鞋子，她存了些钱，希望能买得起。到了鞋店，奶奶查看鞋子价格后，因价格过高而沉重地坐了下来，孩子以为是标价写错了，奶奶却摇头表示价格没错。
[P8] 孩子和奶奶为了寻找他渴望的那双运动鞋，接连去了三家二手商店，但前两家都没有找到，直到第三家店的橱窗里，孩子看到了一个让他感兴趣的物品。
[P9] 在第三家二手商店，孩子发现了一双黑色带白色斜纹的高帮鞋，标价2.50美元，他非常兴奋。奶奶称赞鞋子，孩子试穿后觉得合适，尽管他不知道具体尺码。
[P10] 奶奶为孩子试穿新鞋，担心不合脚而拒绝购买。孩子自己用积蓄买下鞋子，尽管不合脚，仍一瘸一拐地走向公共汽车站。
[P11] 几天后，奶奶在主角的衣橱里放了一双新靴子，对主角之前买的不合脚的鞋子没有多说什么。主角安慰奶奶说鞋子会越穿越大，奶奶随后拥抱了他。
[P12] 主角发现新买的鞋子没有变大，只好换回旧鞋上学。在数学课上，他注意到同学安东尼奥的鞋子也破旧，脚比自己小。放学后，他独自去公园思考，发现安东尼奥也在那里，他是唯一没有嘲笑他穿旧鞋的同学。
[P13] 主角和同学安东尼奥在操场上玩耍，主角因安东尼奥鞋子上的胶带松动而感到困扰，表达了不想这样的心情。两人在奔跑后，安东尼奥询问主角具体不想什么。
[P14] 主角邀请同学安东尼奥共进晚餐，安东尼奥发现了主角新买的鞋子并表现出羡慕。主角感到不安，当晚辗转难眠，第二天早上最后一次穿上了那双鞋子。
[P15] 主角在雪中将新买的鞋子放在同学安东尼奥家门口，按响门铃后迅速跑开。
[P16] 在学校，主角看到安东尼奥穿着新鞋很开心，但对自己的旧鞋感到沮丧。下课时，因雪天需换靴子，主角想起自己有新靴子，安东尼奥感谢他，主角笑着轻轻推了他一下。
[P17] 两个孩子在雪地里奔跑，其中一个提议比赛谁跑得快。
